misconceptions.description: Running a design clinic on surface attributes instead of the chain from learner action to principle to revision
misconceptions.trigger: clinic questions ask about fonts, time spent, or whether it looks finished
misconceptions.feedback: Ask the author to trace one screen from learner action to principle to revision. Polish is the last layer, not the clinic's focus.

misconceptions.description: Giving clinic feedback as personal preference with no tie to learner need, principle, or evidence
misconceptions.trigger: reviewer says I would have done it differently without a reason the author can act on
misconceptions.feedback: Name the learner consequence and the principle behind a suggested change. Preference alone gives the author nothing to evaluate.

misconceptions.description: Treating a generic AI critique as a verdict rather than a prompt for self-review against your own learners and goals
misconceptions.trigger: learner adopts AI suggestions wholesale without verifying them against the draft
misconceptions.feedback: Bring only the AI points you can substantiate in your own draft with evidence. Generic critique does not know your learners.

misconceptions.description: Producing a revision plan as a flat list of unrelated fixes with no tie back to the problem statement or evidenced impact
misconceptions.trigger: plan lists every possible improvement with no priority or connection to the learner outcome
misconceptions.feedback: Rank revisions by evidenced impact on the named learner outcome and connect each back to the problem statement.
